definition: so different from each other that they cannot be easily compared or combined

collocations.example: The committee united several disparate groups behind one shared goal.
She blended disparate elements into a single coherent design.

definition: to make a feeling, belief, or idea disappear

collocations.example: The company acted quickly to dispel the rumors.
Her calm explanation helped dispel our doubts about the plan.

definition: to cut open a dead body or plant in order to study its parts

collocations.example: In biology class we had to dissect a frog.
The students carefully dissect each specimen during the lab.

definition: a long piece of writing on a subject, done for a university degree

collocations.example: She is finishing her doctoral dissertation this spring.
He spent two years writing a dissertation on medieval trade.

definition: to spread out and gradually disappear, or to make something do this

collocations.example: The large fins help dissipate heat from the engine.
These brakes dissipate energy as they slow the car.

definition: the official ending of an organization, agreement, or marriage

collocations.example: The dissolution of the company left many employees jobless.

definition: the quality or state of being a god or being divine

definition: showing stubborn determination and refusing to give up

His dogged persistence finally won the difficult contract.

definition: the power or right to rule or control something

definition: to put on a piece of clothing

collocations.example: He paused to don a coat before heading outside.
The guards don a uniform before each shift.

definition: used to emphasize that something, usually bad, is completely true

collocations.example: The waiter was downright rude to every customer.

definition: to sleep lightly, especially for a short time during the day

collocations.example: Some students often doze off during long lectures.
Grandpa likes to doze in a chair after lunch.

definition: a slow way of speaking in which the vowel sounds are longer than usual

collocations.example: She spoke in a slow southern drawl.
He answered my question with a lazy drawl.

definition: to remove mud and dirt from the bottom of a river, harbor, or lake

collocations.example: Workers dredge the harbor to keep ships moving safely.

definition: a piece of bedroom furniture with drawers, often with a mirror

collocations.example: She keeps her jewelry in the bedroom dresser.
He left his keys in the top dresser drawer.

definition: to move a ball along by bouncing or tapping it, as in basketball

He dribbled past two defenders and made an easy layup.

definition: light rain falling in very fine drops

collocations.example: A light drizzle fell steadily throughout the morning.
We walked home through a cold, fine drizzle.

definition: an aircraft without a pilot that is controlled from the ground

collocations.example: He learned to fly a drone over the fields.
The company tested a delivery drone for small packages.

definition: to hang or bend downward, especially from tiredness or weakness

definition: a woman of very high social rank, or the wife of a duke

definition: two people who perform or work together as a pair

definition: the state of not working or operating normally

definition: the movement of the tide as it flows back away from the land

definition: based on the belief that all people are equal and deserve equal rights

collocations.example: They dream of building a truly egalitarian society.

definition: to force someone to leave a place, especially using physical force

collocations.example: Security had to eject a fan from the stadium.
Officials used guards to eject the noisy protesters.

definition: a conductor through which electricity enters or leaves a device or substance

definition: relating to the connection between electric currents and magnetic fields

collocations.example: Power lines create a strong electromagnetic field around them.
Radio waves are a form of electromagnetic radiation.

definition: a large tree with rough, broad leaves, common in Europe and America

collocations.example: A tall elm tree shaded the entire garden.
The old table was made from solid elm wood.

definition: to make something longer, or to become longer

collocations.example: Vertical stripes elongate the shape of the figure.
Certain stretches help elongate the body and improve posture.

definition: to escape from or avoid someone or something, often in a clever way

collocations.example: The thief managed to elude the police for weeks.
The fugitive used disguises to elude capture.

definition: to free someone from legal, social, or political restrictions

collocations.example: The new law helped emancipate thousands of slaves.
The movement fought to emancipate women from unfair laws.

definition: to make something more attractive by adding decorative details

collocations.example: She chose to embellish the dress with tiny beads.
The craftsmen embellish the box with gold patterns.

definition: a design or object that represents a particular group, idea, or quality

collocations.example: The eagle serves as the country's national emblem.
The dove is a well-known emblem of peace.

definition: a bright green precious stone used in jewelry

collocations.example: She wore a beautiful emerald ring on her finger.
The jeweler showed us a large, polished emerald.

definition: a hard, shiny coating applied to metal or pottery for protection or decoration

collocations.example: The pot has a smooth enamel coating inside.
They finished the door with glossy white enamel paint.

definition: a small area or group that is different from the larger area surrounding it

collocations.example: The city has a lively ethnic enclave downtown.

definition: to gradually move into or take someone else's space, rights, or time

definition: a book or online resource giving information on many subjects or topics

collocations.example: Students often check an online encyclopedia for quick facts.
She wrote a detailed encyclopedia entry about whales.

definition: to make someone be liked by or popular with other people

definition: to cause a feeling, situation, or condition to exist or develop

definition: to surround and cover someone or something completely

Rising flood waters threatened to engulf the small village.

definition: a person or company that enters a competition or newly joins a field

Every competition entrant must register before Friday.

definition: an official who represents a government in dealings with another country

collocations.example: The president sent a special envoy to the talks.
A peace envoy traveled to the region last week.

definition: the imaginary line around the middle of the earth, equally distant from both poles

collocations.example: Countries near the equator stay warm all year.
The ship will cross the equator tomorrow morning.

definition: a short trip made to do a specific task, often for someone else

collocations.example: She asked me to run an errand downtown.
They sent him on a fool's errand across town.

definition: not regular or predictable; changing suddenly and without reason

collocations.example: His erratic behavior worried his family and friends.
The police stopped her for erratic driving.

definition: incorrect or based on a mistake

definition: to support or adopt a belief, cause, or way of life

collocations.example: Few politicians dared to espouse such a risky cause.
The writer continued to espouse controversial political views.

definition: to cause someone to become unfriendly or separated from another person

collocations.example: The argument served to estrange him from his family.

definition: the wide part of a river where it flows into the sea

collocations.example: Many birds feed along the river estuary at dawn.
The tidal estuary floods twice every day.

definition: a system of moral principles or a standard of behavior

collocations.example: Her strong work ethic impressed every manager.
A strict professional ethic guides every doctor's decisions.

definition: the characteristic spirit, values, and beliefs of a group or community

collocations.example: Teamwork is central to the whole company ethos.
The school ethos encourages kindness and hard work.

definition: to demand and obtain something, especially by force or authority

collocations.example: The long war exacted a terrible price from both nations.
He waited years to exact revenge on his rival.

definition: a short passage taken from a longer book, film, or piece of music

collocations.example: She read an excerpt from her new novel.
The teacher played a short excerpt of the song.

definition: to strongly encourage or urge someone to do something

collocations.example: The coach exhorted the players to try even harder.
The speaker exhorted the crowd to vote.

definition: so serious that it threatens the continued existence of something

definition: a situation in which many people leave a place at the same time

definition: a quick and convenient method used to achieve a particular result

collocations.example: The tent was only a temporary expedient until repairs finished.

definition: to use or spend energy, money, time, or effort

definition: a clear and detailed explanation of an idea or theory

collocations.example: The book offers a clear exposition of economic theory.
His lecture gave a detailed exposition of the method.

definition: the act of officially forcing someone to leave a place or organization

collocations.example: Cheating led to his expulsion from school.
The students could face expulsion for breaking the rules.

definition: to cause a fire or light to stop burning

collocations.example: The firefighters worked hard to extinguish the fire.
She leaned over to extinguish the candle before bed.

definition: to officially send an accused person to another country for trial

collocations.example: A judge agreed to extradite him to the United States.
The government refused to extradite the suspect.

definition: the spending of too much money, or something that costs more than is needed

collocations.example: His financial extravagance eventually ruined the family business.
A weekend trip was her only small extravagance.

definition: full of energy, excitement, and happiness

collocations.example: Her exuberant personality lit up the whole room.
The fans were in an exuberant mood after winning.

definition: a short story, often with animals, that teaches a moral lesson

collocations.example: The classic fable warns against lying to others.
She told the children a fable about a clever fox.

definition: the front, outer face of a building

collocations.example: The office tower has a sleek glass facade.
The city paid to restore the cathedral's facade.

definition: a situation or event that is absurd and badly organized

collocations.example: The disorganized trial became a complete farce.
The meeting quickly turned into a farce.

definition: a political system with a powerful dictator and strict control of the people

collocations.example: Historians study the rise of fascism in Europe.
Many soldiers gave their lives to fight fascism.

definition: to understand something difficult after careful thought

collocations.example: We are trying to fathom out what went wrong.
His strange decision was very hard to fathom.

definition: all the animals living in a particular region or period

collocations.example: The island's flora and fauna attract many scientists.
The guide described the local fauna in great detail.

definition: to go through a chemical change in which sugar becomes alcohol or acid

definition: very fierce, violent, or aggressive

collocations.example: The lion is a ferocious animal when it is hungry.

definition: to search for and discover something hidden after careful effort

collocations.example: Reporters worked hard to ferret out the truth.
The team tried to ferret out the missing details.

definition: showing very strong and sincere feelings about something

collocations.example: She is a fervent supporter of animal rights.
It is my fervent hope that peace will come.

definition: relating to an unborn baby developing inside the womb

collocations.example: Good nutrition supports healthy fetal development during pregnancy.
He curled up in the fetal position to stay warm.

definition: a long and bitter argument between two people or groups

collocations.example: The old family feud lasted for three generations.
A bitter feud developed between the two companies.

definition: relating to the medieval system in which people worked land owned by lords

collocations.example: In feudal society, peasants served powerful landowners.

definition: the last part of a performance, show, or series of events

collocations.example: Fireworks lit the sky during the grand finale.
Millions watched the dramatic season finale last night.

definition: to think or worry about one thing far too much

collocations.example: Try not to fixate on things you cannot change.

definition: a natural talent or ability for doing something well

collocations.example: She has a real flair for languages.

definition: a very small jumping insect that feeds on the blood of animals

The cat tried to catch a flea in its fur.

definition: to make a sudden small movement because of fear or pain

collocations.example: She didn't flinch at the loud, sudden noise.

definition: a sudden short period of intense activity or excitement

collocations.example: Her arrival caused a flurry of activity in the office.

definition: a set of letters and symbols printed in one particular style and size

collocations.example: Please increase the font size for easier reading.
The headings appear in a large bold font.

definition: film or video recording of a particular event

collocations.example: Police reviewed the video footage of the accident.
The channel showed live footage from the stadium.

definition: to search widely for food or other supplies

collocations.example: The deer forage for food in the early morning.
The pigs forage in the woods for acorns.

definition: a worker who is in charge of a group of other workers

collocations.example: The site foreman checked everyone's safety equipment.
The factory foreman reported the problem to the manager.

definition: to lose or give up something as a penalty for doing something wrong

collocations.example: If you cancel the room, you will forfeit your deposit.

definition: having an important and lasting influence on someone's development

collocations.example: She spent her formative years growing up in Miami.

definition: an entrance hall or open area near the entrance of a building

collocations.example: Journalists waited in the hotel foyer for hours.
